title: Practice in the test's format
statement: Whether practice and mastery checks should share formats, or practice should mostly differ from the final test on purpose, with test-format practice saved for the end.
detail: A direct-instruction BrainLift given to the reading course plans says items in mastery tests should match the formats met during instruction (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/feedback/feedback1/Direct Instruction BrainLift.md`). The plans' own review gauntlet asks whether early practice looks like the test and answers that it mostly shouldn't: vocabulary in context, monitoring prompts and knowledge work, with test-format practice late and timed conditions last (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/skills/train-teacher/references/gauntlet-spec.md`). The alignment plan lists the two as an open tension and proposes a reading under which both hold, familiar formats on unfamiliar passages, still to be confirmed (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/docs/academics-alignment-plan.md`).

evidence.quote: - You should ensure test items in mastery tests match the formats experienced during instruction.
does early practice look like the test? (It mostly shouldn't — vocabulary-in-context, monitoring prompts, knowledge work; test-format practice concentrated late, timed conditions last.)
compatible read: format familiarity + passage coldness. Confirm.
Mastery tests should match formats experienced during instruction.
Assessment format is not instruction format (the marathon rule)
Format familiarity is measurement hygiene, not test prep (construct-irrelevant variance, AERA/APA/NCME Standard 1.13).
